name: Dr Elijah Harmon's Cabin

documented_range.note: 'HIS RESIDENCE WAS A CABIN OF HEWN LOGS' - Andreas's medical chapter, in the passage that also gives Harmon's rusty instruments, his hundred books and his larder of flour, bacon and coffee. The fabric and the use are documented; the far end of the range is inferred, and note that the household's own presence on the scene date is recorded as UNCERTAIN because Harmon may have been in Texas. The cabin does not move when its owner does.

change_note: The building as this dataset can state it on the scene date. Where the sources give a size, a plan or a fabric, the record carries it; where they do not, the note says so attribute by attribute.

placement.position_note: INVENTED. No source places Harmon's cabin. What is known is negative: he pre-empted a hundred and forty acres whose northern boundary was near Sixteenth Street, which is two kilometres south of the modelled ground and is a farm rather than a residence. This record sits in the South Division outer band where the reconstruction recipes put older log dwellings, at the first free position the placement rule found. It is a guess inside the right district.

footprint.note: PLACEHOLDER - NO DIMENSION IS ATTESTED. 20 x 26 ft is the schedule's D1 older-log-cabin band: one room and a loft, which is what a doctor's residence-and-surgery would have been in a town this size. Every number is invented.

persons.name: Dr Elijah Dewey Harmon
persons.note: HIS STOCK IN TRADE IS DESCRIBED AND IT IS THE MOST CONCRETE MATERIAL DETAIL ABOUT ANY PERSON IN THIS PARCEL: 'A case of rusty instruments, a library of about one hundred volumes and a stock of medicines brought from the Green Mountains ... His residence was a cabin of hewn logs; his larder, a repository of flour, bacon and coffee.' Born at Bennington, Vermont, 20 August 1782; married Welthyan Loomis 30 October 1808; volunteer surgeon aboard the Saratoga at Plattsburg in 1814. He pre-empted one hundred and forty acres whose northern boundary was near Sixteenth Street. THE FEDERAL LAND TRACT SALES — A PURCHASE, AND NEVER A RESIDENCE. The Illinois State Archives' Public Domain Land Tract Sales register enters this person 2 times, as “HARMON ELIJAH D”, 1834-10-02: 1 federal land entry — SWFR sec 22 T39N R14E, 276.48 acres stated in all, for $345.60 (ls0435, ls0436). THE REGISTER'S OWN RESIDENCE COLUMN READS COOK, UNKNOWN on these rows: a county, a state or nothing, and never a town, which is why a purchase here places nobody. A purchase and nothing more. It dates and places a transaction; it proposes no residence, and under the ratified ladder it corroborates rather than mints. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: HARMON ELIJAH D matches Dr Elijah Dewey Harmon: the forename names Dr Elijah Dewey Harmon of the 5 people of this surname, and the forename agrees in full. (data/research/land_sales/resident_crosswalk.json). This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a second independent source is what lifts a projected resident, and a land entry is a second source about a TRANSACTION rather than about who was living at Chicago on 1 July 1835 — a man may buy a quarter-section he never sees. T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once; this pass hands it the evidence and not the verdict.

residents.research_note: A DOCUMENTED RESIDENT WHO MAY HAVE BEEN IN TEXAS, kept in the dataset precisely because the presence field can say so. Dropping him would lose the town's first doctor, his hewn-log cabin, his hundred books and the only stated economic motive in the parcel; asserting him would be a claim the source contradicts. HIS FAMILY IS THE REASON THE HOUSEHOLD MATTERS ANYWAY: the Harmon brothers' dry-goods firm is a separate household here, Harmon Court is named for him, and his daughter Mrs A. G. Burley supplied Andreas with these particulars fifty years later - which is a useful reminder that a good deal of what looks like documentation in this book is family recollection with a name attached.
